rationale: The shed camera's RSSI is -87 dBm, below the -80 dBm threshold that causes intermittent disconnections and choppy live view. The customer confirmed the shed is detached ~25m away with a new metal fence in the signal path, and the repositioning test (holding the camera at the back door) streamed perfectly, confirming the camera itself is not defective. This is an L1 signal-range issue, not a hardware fault warranting replacement.

repair_steps: Advise customer to reposition the shed camera closer to the house or with a clearer line of sight to the base station, avoiding the metal fence.
If repositioning is not possible, recommend installing the official RP-1 repeater between the base station and the shed to boost signal strength.
After repositioning or installing repeater, verify the camera's RSSI in Device Settings > Device Info is above -80 dBm (ideally above -70 dBm).
Confirm live view is stable and no further disconnections occur over the next 24 hours.

args.query: weak signal camera intermittent offline RSSI fix procedure

results.text: Customer reported a CAM-S1 in a detached garage going offline several times a day. RSSI was -86 dBm; all other devices normal. Installing an RP-1 repeater solved it. Resolved at frontline.

Peripherals talk to the base station over a sub-GHz proprietary radio. Signal strength (RSSI) is shown in Device Settings > Device Info. Above -70 dBm is good, -70 to -80 dBm is acceptable, below -80 dBm causes intermittent disconnections, delayed notifications and choppy live view. Concrete walls, metal doors and fridges strongly attenuate the signal. Fix: move the device or base station, or install the official RP-1 repeater.
